multiseed_null_methodology.UNDERPOWERED_CORRELATION_PATTERN: THIRD OCCURRENCE IN THIS LEDGER. S1614: rho .6727 at p .0192 on 10 classes, called REAL AT POWER; S1616 got rho .0182 at p .9601 on 10 disjoint classes. S1643: rho .657 at p .0875 on 6 classes, explicitly flagged UNDERPOWERED; S1644 got rho .0559 at p .434 on 12. The flag is what made the second case a correction rather than a retraction. multiseed_null_methodology.S1647_S1648_THE_EIGENVALUE_RATIO: THE ARC'S ONLY POSITIVE, AND IT IS NOT CERTIFIED. After S1644/S1646 killed every predictor of causal cost tested in-sample, the eigenvalue RATIO |lam1/lam2| of the class-projected quadratic -- computable from WEIGHTS ALONE, no rows, no forward passes, no 20-basis null -- was registered as a SINGLE hypothesis and tested on classes it was never fitted on. Set 1 (12 function words, S1647): rho +.6783, permutation p .019, 12/12 positive CE rise. Set 2 (12 TYPE-SPANNING classes, S1648): rho +.5105, p .094, 9/12 positive. POOLED (n=24, same pre-registered hypothesis, neither set used for selection): rho +.4157 at p .0452. Pooled rho sits BELOW both components because Spearman on the union re-ranks across sets whose CE-rise scales differ -- heterogeneity costs correlation while doubled n buys power.
multiseed_null_methodology.WHY_S1647_IS_NOT_PROMOTED: CAUTION 1 IS UNDISCHARGED. S1647's rho .6783 at p .0186 on n=12 sits almost exactly on S1614's rho .6727 at p .0192 on n=10, which S1616 then refuted at rho .0182 / p .9601 on disjoint classes. The structural difference is real -- S1614 was IN-SAMPLE while S1647/S1648 are out-of-sample against a hypothesis registered before each run, which is the protection S1614 lacked -- but this ledger has been fooled at exactly this magnitude and scale before. Two pre-registered held-out sets are better evidence than S1614 ever had and are still not a certified result.
multiseed_null_methodology.SLICE_CONSTRUCTION_LIMIT: The ablation cost VANISHES for very broad classes. In S1648: `cap` (7156 scored positions, 10735 vocabulary tokens) gives relative CE rise -.0008 and `digit` (1702 positions, 1691 tokens) gives +.00004. A rank-2 slice cannot carry much about a class spanning thousands of vocabulary items, so there is little for a mean-ablation to remove. This is a limit on the SLICE CONSTRUCTION, not on the ratio hypothesis, and it predicts the effect should vanish for any sufficiently broad class.
multiseed_null_methodology.CURRENCY_CORRECTION_HOLDS: S1645's fix -- score RELATIVE CE rise (rise / that class's own base CE) rather than absolute -- continues to hold. rho(n_positions, relative rise) is -.098 on set 1 and +.0000 on set 2, across classes spanning 97 to 7156 positions. The absolute-rise confound that dominated S1644 (rho -.580) does not return under the corrected currency.

what_it_computes.reading: mlp0 does NOT re-encode the token -- the embedding never leaves the residual stream. It computes the token's CLASS: ~360 distinct tokens collapse into a ~23-dim space, 6x below the embedding. And it does so NONLINEARLY -- that class structure is only 44% linearly predictable from the embedding it is computed from. STANDING PREDICTION: any affine/linear read of mlp0 caps out low. Codex's v1 affine compiler independently hit this (QNN +0.010, 11.2% of its oracle).

what_reads_it.reading: mlp4 reads the CLASS-CODE tier, not the token table. mlp0 is its dominant input at 1.8x mlp3.

coupling.reading: The early block is a COUPLED causal program: joint live MLP0+1+2 restoration gains .5115 nats against a singleton sum of .0573 -- 8.9x superadditive, and MLP2 FLIPS SIGN after upstream repair. mlp0 cannot be understood or compiled in isolation from mlp1/mlp2.

what_the_residue_is_NOT.reading: The context residual is NOT previous-token: its share (.2068) is at or below its own null (.2115). A prev-token feature does not explain what the table cannot.

Large-effect substitutions compose near-additively; small-effect ones sit near 2.1 regardless of family, because the interaction term does not shrink with the individual terms. ANY composition ratio quoted without holding effect size fixed is reporting how big the individual effects happened to be.

One doubling does not establish a rate, and the front modules are not representative of the middle fourteen, which §1326 puts below the instrument's floor. TESTABLE, NOT TESTED.

_front_band_account.implications_for_a_bottom_up_compiler: 1. Target mlp1 first if the goal is nats: 6.997 against 2.19 for mlp0+mlp2+mlp3 combined. 2. Target mlp0 first if the goal is UNDERSTANDING: it is small, near the tokens, computes a 23-dim class code, and everything above reads it (mlp4 takes .674 dCE from mlp0, §1422). 3. Prefer TABLE-family components where composition matters -- they are the only family measured to compose additively, and refitting them against each other makes things WORSE not better. 4. Do not certify any front module in isolation: §1616's 8.9x superadditivity and §1485's mlp2 brittleness are both local!=composite failures at module grain. 5. A priced frontier already exists for mlp1 (.9624 @ 214 Mbit, §1480) and a cheap repair for mlp2 (1.8 Mbit recovers .80 CE, §1489) -- place new programs against these, not in a vacuum. PROTOCOL WARNING: ladder-protocol numbers throughout; §1324 warns they do not compare to exact-restoration denominators. Three incompatible mlp0 values exist. Never mix denominators.

_composition_ratios_are_effect_size_conf.finding: S1657: joint/sum composition ratios track TOTAL EFFECT SIZE, not substitution family. Measured at four front MLPs, same rows, same cost definition: sum 2.55 -> ratio 1.03; sum 2.19 -> 1.15; sum 0.66 -> 2.14; sum 0.055 -> 2.16. At matched effect size a PROJECTION composed BETTER than a TABLE (1.029 vs 1.153), inverting the family distinction I had asserted.
_composition_ratios_are_effect_size_conf.mechanism: joint/sum has a denominator that shrinks faster than its numerator as individual effects get small, because the interaction term does not shrink proportionally. This follows from the ratio's algebra, so the DIRECTION is protocol-robust even though the magnitude is not.
_composition_ratios_are_effect_size_conf.rule: NEVER quote or compare a composition ratio without holding total effect size fixed, and never compare ratios measured in different protocols. S1656 did both and cost three withdrawn board posts.

ratios_in_this_ledger_and_their_effect_s.S541 six blocks, rank truncation: ratio 1.6, effect size NOT recorded here -- check before comparing
ratios_in_this_ledger_and_their_effect_s.S1616 three modules, exact restoration: ratio 8.9x at singleton sum 0.0573 -- a SMALL-effect sum, so part of that 8.9x may be the same artifact. FLAGGED, not withdrawn: it is a different protocol and I am not repeating S1656 by assuming my curve transfers.

_composition_ratios_are_effect_size_conf.TOTAL_GLASS_IS_NOT_AFFECTED: S1658 checked the benchmark headline series. As the ship improves its total effect shrinks (1.610 -> 1.176 -> 0.900) while compounding FALLS (1.43 -> 1.04 -> 0.80). The artifact pushes ratios UP as effects shrink, so the observed trend runs OPPOSITE to it and cannot be produced by it. v4 sub-additivity stands; the improvement was if anything MASKED. The confound is CONSERVATIVE here: equal compounding at a smaller total effect is a real gain, not a plateau.

_mlp0_dossier_resolved.claim: mlp0 is 90.27% reproducible by a current-token lookup table in the running model (covered-position, hybrid-substitution protocol). The remaining 9.73% (0.083 nats) is cross-position information, which in a transformer necessarily arrives via attention.

measurement.protocol: per-token mean table for mlp0, fit skip1200 / eval skip7000, positions>=64; HYBRID substitution (table only at covered positions, mlp0 LIVE elsewhere); CE scored on covered positions only; ablation baseline = optimal constant from opt_ablation_consts_all.pt

instrument_check.known_answer_derivation: attn0 frozen at a constant => residual stream below mlp0 is embedding+constant => mlp0 is position-wise deterministic in the current token => a covered table must be exact => ceiling must be 1.0

_mlp0_dossier_resolved.not_claimed: the 100% frozen ceiling is a CHECK, not a discovery -- with attn0 constant mlp0 is a token function by construction. The finding is the live arm's 90.27% and the fact that freezing one module accounts for the entire remainder.
_mlp0_dossier_resolved.supersedes: two earlier versions of this measurement (S1659) whose instrument check failed; neither was reported
_mlp0_dossier_resolved.CORRECTION_S1662: The original wording claimed '100% of the residue is attn0's write' as an empirical attribution. It is not: attention is the only module that moves information across positions, so an MLP with its attention inputs frozen is token-deterministic BY CONSTRUCTION and its covered table is exact NECESSARILY. The frozen arm is an instrument check, not evidence of attribution. The empirical content is the live 90.27% split. WHICH attention delivers the residue is a real open question and is not answered here.
_mlp0_dossier_resolved.claim_ORIGINAL: mlp0 is ~90% a current-token lookup table, and 100% of the remaining residue is context delivered by attn0. mlp0 computes no context-dependence of its own.

_position_wise_masking_cannot_isolate.claim: In a transformer, excluding positions from a CE average does NOT isolate a position-wise substitution applied at those positions: the wrong values propagate upward and attention mixes them into the retained positions. Interventions must be restricted in the FORWARD PASS, not repaired in the score.
_position_wise_masking_cannot_isolate.evidence: on a quantity with an analytically known answer of 1.0: substitute-everywhere + mask-score gave 0.5583; substitute-only-where-valid gave 1.0000. A 44-point error.

_front_band_tables_are_low_rank.protocol: per-token table, SVD centred on the position-weighted mean with rows scaled by sqrt(count) so truncation minimises POSITION-weighted error; S1661 hybrid substitution; covered-position scoring
_front_band_tables_are_low_rank.replicates: S780's effective rank 22.7 for mlp0 -- rank 23 reaches 89.24% of its full table. Also replicates all four S1662 full-table ceilings to the digit.

_middle_band_is_redundant_not_small.S1657_caution: the 4.26x ratio must NOT be compared against the front band's 1.15; composition ratios track total effect size
_middle_band_is_redundant_not_small.PENDING_protocol_match: the 21.73% joint ceiling is NOT yet comparable to the front band's 68-96% PER-SITE ceilings; band_joint_compare.py re-measures both as joint substitutions under one protocol

_middle_band_program_family_prices.why_the_remainder_is_meaningful: bilin18's MLPs are pure bilinear with no elementwise nonlinearity, so 1 - (full-rank linear ceiling) prices what the quadratic form does that no linear map of the same input can imitate -- it is not approximation error
_middle_band_program_family_prices.coverage_control: a linear map has no coverage gap; scoring the linear arms both all-positions and covered-only differs by at most 3.49% across the curve, so the table's 21.73% and the 40-point family gap are not coverage artifacts
_middle_band_program_family_prices.protocol: joint substitution over the band, covered-position scoring, optimal-constant stake -- identical to S1666 so the numbers compare

MIDDLE (mlp4-15) is linear-ish and the most bilinear: linear 62.33% vs token 21.73%, quadratic remainder 37.67%. LATE (mlp16-17) is nearly a linear readout: linear 83.60%, quadratic remainder only 16.40%.
_program_family_table_by_band.control: the middle band replicates S1667's 62.33% to the digit within the same execution
_program_family_table_by_band.failed_prediction_a: predicted the front band would be more linear than tabular like the middle; it is the REVERSE by 7.8 points. Any 'linear beats table at whole-stack scale' comparison is PENDING the compiled-table arm.
_program_family_table_by_band.RESOLVED_S1670: the compiled all-table figure is 49.96% (not the naive 34.27%). Linear still wins at whole-stack scale but by 4.3 points, not 20. The band regimes transfer: a mixed compiled program reaches 56.29%.

_joint_substitution_compounds_off_distri.claim: A substitution fitted against the real model and applied jointly at many sites compounds off-distribution and past some number of sites returns a NEGATIVE ceiling (worse than constant ablation). 12 sites: 62.33%. 18 sites: -42.99%.

_joint_substitution_compounds_off_distri.usable_arms: the full-rank arm (no truncation error, isolates compounding alone) and single-band arms small enough to stay stable
_joint_substitution_compounds_off_distri.prior_art: S546 found the opposite remedy also fails -- refitting block 1 against an already-substituted block 0 cost +1.0647 vs +0.6654 naive. Neither naive nor refitted composition is safe by default.

_bottom_up_compilation_is_required.claim: Substituting all 18 MLPs with linear maps of the residual stream scores -42.99% when each map is fitted against the real model, and 54.28% when compiled bottom-up (each site fitted with everything below already substituted). Compilation is a requirement at scale, not an optimisation.
_bottom_up_compilation_is_required.control: on the middle band, where naive fitting already worked, compilation moves the ceiling +0.76 points -- so the +97 points at 18 sites is compounding removed, not a generically better procedure
_bottom_up_compilation_is_required.headline: eighteen linear maps compiled bottom-up reproduce 54.28% of bilin18's entire MLP stake (4.32 nats) -- the first program in this ledger covering every MLP
_bottom_up_compilation_is_required.S546_does_not_generalise: S546 found refitting made a 2-block TABLE substitution WORSE (+1.0647 vs +0.6654). Family and scale both differ, so 'refitting hurts' is false as a general rule and the reason it held at S546 is UNRESOLVED.

_best_compiled_program_for_mlp_stack.claim: Two figures, answering different questions. STANDALONE (the program fully replaces the MLPs at every position): eighteen least-squares linear maps of the residual stream, compiled bottom-up, reproduce 54.28% of bilin18's 4.3196-nat MLP stake. UNDER THE COVERED-POSITION PROTOCOL used throughout this ledger (module left live at the 23.4% of positions whose token was unseen at fit): linear 57.99% > token tables at mlp0-2 57.29% > additive 54.35%.
_best_compiled_program_for_mlp_stack.control: the all-linear arm reproduces S1669's 54.28% exactly
_best_compiled_program_for_mlp_stack.out_of_sample_confirmation: S1668's band regimes (front tabular, middle/late linear) were derived from separate per-band measurements. Applying each band's winning family inside one compiled whole-stack program beats both pure families -- the regimes transfer and predict an improvement outside the measurement that produced them.
_best_compiled_program_for_mlp_stack.corrects: S1668's naive all-table figure of 34.27% was substantially a statement about fitting order; compilation lifts the table family 15.7 points. Made properly the family gap is 4.3 points, not 20.
_best_compiled_program_for_mlp_stack.SUPERSEDED_BY_S1672: the best pure assignment is tables at mlp0-2 (57.29%), not mlp0-3 (56.29%). Adding mlp3 to the table set COSTS a point.
_best_compiled_program_for_mlp_stack.claim_ORIGINAL: bilin18's entire MLP stack is 56.29% reproduced by a compiled 18-piece program: per-token lookup tables at mlp0-3 and least-squares linear maps of the residual stream at mlp4-17, fitted bottom-up in stack order. This beats both pure families (all-linear 54.28%, all-table 49.96%).
_best_compiled_program_for_mlp_stack.claim_ORIGINAL_S1672: bilin18's entire MLP stack is 57.29% reproduced by a compiled 18-piece program: per-token lookup tables at mlp0-2 and least-squares linear maps at mlp3-17, fitted bottom-up in stack order (S1672). Beats all-linear 54.28% and the mlp0-3 variant 56.29%.
_best_compiled_program_for_mlp_stack.CORRECTION_S1674: I quoted 57.29% as 'the best program' from S1670 onward. The hybrid hook leaves the module LIVE at uncovered positions -- a genuine artifact limitation for a TABLE (which has no entry there) but simply 'not substituting' for a LINEAR MAP (which is defined everywhere). Family comparisons stay fair since every arm leaves the same positions live, but the absolute figure overstates a standalone program. STRUCTURAL ASYMMETRY: there is no standalone table program at all -- a table substituted everywhere is the arm LESSONS 27 showed is broken. A linear map can be a program; a lookup table can only be an account of the positions it covers.

_compiled_program_residual_is_diffuse.claim: The 43.71% missing from the best compiled MLP-stack program is DIFFUSE, not localised. The worst single site (mlp3) holds 9.91% of the shortfall and fourteen of eighteen sites sit within 0.8 points of each other. There is no bottleneck site.
_compiled_program_residual_is_diffuse.method: the whole stack is RECOMPILED with each site exempted, so the maps above it are never applied off-distribution (LESSONS 28)
_compiled_program_residual_is_diffuse.control: the no-exemption arm reproduces S1670's 56.29% exactly
_compiled_program_residual_is_diffuse.failed_predictions: pred_a predicted concentration (>=25% at one site) and pred_b predicted the worst site would be in the middle band. Both false: 9.91%, and it is mlp3.
_compiled_program_residual_is_diffuse.consequence: the gradient tracks S1662's per-site ceilings (90.27/96.01/76.98/67.55) and exposes that S1670's mlp0-3 table boundary was inherited from a BAND-level verdict over four unlike sites. mlp2 and mlp3 are 77% and 68% tabular and should probably not be tabled.
_compiled_program_residual_is_diffuse.recurring_shape: second diffuse-not-sparse result of the day; S1663 was the first, at head grain inside mlp1
_compiled_program_residual_is_diffuse.measured_in_condition: MEASURED IN THE MLP-ONLY CONDITION (attention running real). S1704 shows this does not transfer: in the JOINT 36-site condition the front-MLP site exemptions are 52% SUPER-additive and their ordering differs from what MLP-only residuals predict, while S1703 finds the joint shortfall concentrated by band. 'Diffuse' is a property of the MLP-only shortfall, not of the joint one.

_per_site_family_not_band_family.claim: Family choice is a PER-SITE property, not a band property. mlp0 and mlp1 want a token table (+1.73 and +1.24 points to the whole-stack program), mlp2 is indifferent (+0.04), and mlp3 actively does not (-1.00). The band-level 'front is tabular' verdict is right about the band and wrong about mlp3.
_per_site_family_not_band_family.corrects: _program_family_table_by_band and the S1670 program, both of which tabled all four front sites on band-level evidence
_per_site_family_not_band_family.measured_in_condition: MEASURED IN THE MLP-ONLY CONDITION (attention running real). The family verdicts still hold there and the mixed program built from them beats both pure families jointly (S1670), but S1704 shows MLP-only per-site quantities do NOT predict joint per-site importance -- residual nats rank mlp1 first while joint exemption gains rank it third.

_local_fidelity_selects_the_wrong_progra.claim: Selecting each site's program family by how well it reconstructs that site's OWN output (position-weighted L2) picks tables at 14 of 18 sites and scores 53.78% end-to-end -- WORSE than using no tables at all (54.28%) and 3.5 points below the best assignment. Local reconstruction fidelity does not predict end-to-end usefulness.
_local_fidelity_selects_the_wrong_progra.mechanism: a token table captures each middle-band site's MEAN output well, which dominates L2, while the directions that matter downstream are ones L2 barely weights
_local_fidelity_selects_the_wrong_progra.implication: any program search that scores candidates against their own module's output is selecting on the wrong quantity -- relevant to lattice/state selection done on local fidelity
_local_fidelity_selects_the_wrong_progra.MECHANISM_UNRESOLVED_S1673: I asserted the mechanism was 'L2 weights directions that do not matter downstream'. That was untested. A simpler account: the greedy criterion was evaluated IN-SAMPLE on the fit rows, where a 6.9M-parameter table beats a 1.3M-parameter linear map by construction. The EMPIRICAL finding is unchanged (local in-sample selection is 3.5 points worse end-to-end than ignoring it); the mechanism is unresolved between these two and should not have been asserted.

_additive_family_loses_to_its_own_specia.claim: The additive program y = b(token) + xW scores 54.35% under matched coverage, BELOW both of its own special cases (all-linear 57.99%, tables-at-mlp0-2 57.29%). Coverage policy is worth 3.71-7.01 points and does not explain it.
_additive_family_loses_to_its_own_specia.design: family (linear|additive|table) x coverage policy (everywhere|hybrid), both reference points reproducing exactly
_additive_family_loses_to_its_own_specia.LEADING_HYPOTHESIS_NOT_A_FINDING: estimation, not expressiveness. The additive arm fits a per-token table at ALL 18 sites -- 6009x1152 parameters from 24576 fit positions, ~4 positions per token. At mlp0-2 the token determines the output (ceilings 90/96/77) so the estimator is sound; at the other fifteen sites b is near noise and W is then fitted on a noisy residual. Adding a term you cannot estimate is worse than omitting it. fit_size_scaling.py tests this at 5x data.
_additive_family_loses_to_its_own_specia.revises: the mechanism asserted in _local_fidelity_selects_the_wrong_program -- see that entry's MECHANISM_UNRESOLVED_S1673 note
_additive_family_loses_to_its_own_specia.S1675_HYPOTHESIS_STILL_OPEN: The fit-size test is CONFOUNDED: the coverage mask is derived from the fit set, so 5x data took coverage from 5419 to 16110 tokens, simultaneously improving estimation and removing the hybrid policy's live-module crutch. Symptom: the LINEAR arm lost 3.29 points on 5x data, which no least-squares fit does. The offset control passed cleanly (<=0.56 points). SUGGESTIVE ONLY: at 480 rows the ordering inverts to table 56.50% > additive 55.02% > linear 54.88%, so the S1673 verdict may be specific to the small fit set. fit_size_fixed_mask.py pins the mask.
_additive_family_loses_to_its_own_specia.RESOLVED_S1676: Hypothesis CONFIRMED with the coverage mask held fixed. From 96 to 480 fit rows the additive family gains +5.29 points, against linear +2.64 and pure table +0.21. Its small-data deficit was estimation, not expressiveness. At 480 rows: linear 60.81%, additive 59.08%, table@mlp0-2 57.16% -- and additive is closing at twice linear's rate, so the ordering is not settled.
_additive_family_loses_to_its_own_specia.S1675_confound_quantified: the linear arm's -3.29 point 'loss' on 5x data becomes a +2.64 point gain once the mask is fixed -- a 5.9-point swing produced entirely by letting coverage grow with the fit set
_additive_family_loses_to_its_own_specia.measured_in_condition: MEASURED IN THE MLP-ONLY CONDITION (attention running real).

_coverage_mask_confounds_fit_size_compar.claim: Under the hybrid substitution policy, the coverage mask is derived from the fit set, so comparisons across fit-set SIZE vary the measurement difficulty at the same time as the estimation quality. More fit data means more coverage, which means fewer positions left live for the real module and a harder task for the program.
_coverage_mask_confounds_fit_size_compar.diagnostic: the linear arm lost 3.29 points going from 96 to 480 fit rows -- a least-squares fit does not get worse with 5x data, so the degradation is the mask
_coverage_mask_confounds_fit_size_compar.fix: hold the coverage mask fixed across fit sizes (same positions substituted, left live, and scored); only then does the comparison isolate estimation
_coverage_mask_confounds_fit_size_compar.clean_result_from_the_same_run: document offset is NOT a variable -- at fixed size, skip1200 vs skip80 moves every family by <=0.56 points

_families_differ_in_their_relation_to_da.claim: The three program families have qualitatively different data dependence, measured with the coverage mask held fixed (96 -> 480 fit rows): the per-token TABLE is SATURATED (+0.21), the LINEAR map is still improving (+2.64), and the ADDITIVE program is data-hungry (+5.29).
_families_differ_in_their_relation_to_da.why_it_matters: the table's saturation is what makes its ceilings statements about bilin18 rather than about the fit -- its limit is that the token does not determine the output, a property of the model. The other two families' measured positions depend on how much data they were given.

_additive_estimation_confirmed_by_trunca.claim: Truncating the token term b to low rank buys the additive program +3.47 points at the small fit set with NO extra data (53.79% -> 57.26% at rank 8). Combined with the +5.29 points from 5x data (S1676), two opposite interventions confirm the deficit is estimation, not expressiveness.
_additive_estimation_confirmed_by_trunca.shape: ranks 8-256 are flat within 0.4 points; only full rank collapses, by 3.5. The harm is concentrated in the tail directions estimated from a handful of token occurrences -- it is not a capacity trade-off with an optimum to tune.
_additive_estimation_confirmed_by_trunca.failed_prediction: pred_b predicted the regularised additive would overtake pure linear at this fit size; it does not (57.26% vs 58.17%). A token term at all 18 sites is not yet worth its estimation cost.
_additive_estimation_confirmed_by_trunca.measured_in_condition: MEASURED IN THE MLP-ONLY CONDITION (attention running real).

_feature_basis_not_sparse_selectable.claim: bilin18's MLPs cannot be described by keeping a subset of their own 4608 bilinear features. Keeping the top 512 by std(h_j)*||Down[:,j]|| and pinning the rest to their means gives a whole-stack ceiling of -49.93% (worse than replacing every MLP with a constant), and the curve is non-monotone. A rotated basis is monotone and strong: 512 of 1152 output principal directions give 94.87%.
_feature_basis_not_sparse_selectable.criterion_is_not_the_problem: top-k beats random by ~80 points, so the ranking is real; both fail anyway
_feature_basis_not_sparse_selectable.mechanism: the readout sums large cancelling contributions; removing either side of a cancelling pair does more damage than the pair was worth
_feature_basis_not_sparse_selectable.CATEGORY_WARNING: the rotated arm still RUNS the MLP and truncates its output; the linear/table/additive programs REPLACE the module. 94.87% is NOT a better program than the linear map's 58.17% -- it answers 'how much of the effect lives in k output directions', not 'how well can a program compute the output without the module'.
_feature_basis_not_sparse_selectable.consequence: any account treating individual bilinear features as units of computation works in a basis where units cannot be removed, while 512 rotated directions capture 95% of the same output. For this model the interpretable decomposition is a subspace, not a feature list.
_feature_basis_not_sparse_selectable.measured_in_condition: Feature selection is applied at all 18 MLPs with ATTENTION RUNNING REAL; the identity checks are exact, but this is not a joint-program measurement.

_program_price_curve.claim: The compiled linear program's price curve: rank 8 gives 41.59% of the 4.33-nat MLP stake for 0.33M reals (1.4% of full cost, 68% of full fidelity); rank 128 gives 54.12% for 5.31M (89% of fidelity, 22% of cost); rank 1152 gives 60.81% for 23.89M. Most fidelity is in the first 128 directions; the last 640 buy 0.4 points for 2.7M reals.
_program_price_curve.validates: the curve is MONOTONE against S1668's non-monotone curve for the same family fitted naively -- the check that S1669's bottom-up compilation fix is real. Identity arm reproduces S1676's 60.81% exactly.
_program_price_curve.failed_prediction: pred_b predicted rank 128 would reach >=90% of full-rank fidelity; it reaches 89.0%
_program_price_curve.measured_in_condition: MEASURED IN THE MLP-ONLY CONDITION (attention running real); the stake is the 4.33-nat MLP stake, not the 5.5684-nat joint stake of S1694.

_passing_predictions_do_not_verify_the_i.claim: A rank sweep returned an identical ceiling at every rank because the truncation was never inserted (a string-patch that matched nothing), and ALL THREE registered predictions passed on the no-op: monotone (constant), 100% of full rank, identity reproduced.
_passing_predictions_do_not_verify_the_i.why_defences_failed: every prediction was a claim about RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN ARMS, which a no-op makes trivially true; and the known-answer instrument check is precisely the arm a no-op gets right
rules: at build time, assert the count of every anchor BEFORE replacing (assert s.count(old)==1) -- asserting a marker afterwards proves the marker, not the edit
at run time, any parameter sweep must assert its arms are not all identical
_passing_predictions_do_not_verify_the_i.general_shape: predictions constrain the SCIENCE, instrument checks constrain the MEASUREMENT, neither constrains whether the INTERVENTION was applied

_attention_output_write_is_nonlocal.claim: A position-wise least-squares linear map of the current position's residual stream recovers 16.38% of bilin18's eighteen attention OUTPUT WRITES (3.5570-nat stake), against 60.81% for the MLP stack. The attention output write is 83.6% NON-LOCAL: five sixths of what it contributes cannot be computed from the current position at all.
_attention_output_write_is_nonlocal.protocol: bottom-up compilation (S1669), coverage mask pinned to n96_skip80 (S1676), covered-position scoring, optimal-constant stake
_attention_output_write_is_nonlocal.SCOPE_output_path_only: each attention module returns (y, v1); the hook substitutes y and passes v1 -- the value embedding threaded to blocks above -- through UNCHANGED. The claim is 'attention's output write replaced', not 'attention replaced'. 83.6% is a FLOOR on the non-locality of the write.
_attention_output_write_is_nonlocal.non_monotone_noted: the curve dips 0.69 points from rank 128 to rank 512/full. Not the sign-flipping collapse LESSONS 28 was written for; ranks 512 and 1152 agree to 5dp so W's effective rank is <=512. Plain reading is rank-128 truncation acting as mild regularisation. The headline is stable across ranks 128-1152 within 0.7 points. Monotonicity was reported, not scored.

_program_numbers_replicate_held_out.claim: Every load-bearing program figure of the S1664-S1682 arc replicates on fineweb_n192_skip11000, documents untouched for the whole arc: all_linear 60.81->60.50, additive 59.08->58.62, table_mlp0_2 57.16->56.25, linear_rank128 54.12->53.98. All deltas within 0.91 points; the family ordering (linear > additive > table) is identical on both sets.
_program_numbers_replicate_held_out.pattern: house second-class confirmation (S1595, S1598, S1603); programs compiled ONCE and scored on both evals
_program_numbers_replicate_held_out.note_on_document_samples: skip11000 is EASIER to predict (CE live 3.097 vs 3.292) yet its MLPs matter MORE (stake 4.517 vs 4.330). The ceiling is a ratio within its own eval set; both stakes are reported so the 0.19-nat difference in what the ratio is a fraction of is visible.
_program_numbers_replicate_held_out.not_claimed: no story is offered for the ordering of the four generalisation gaps -- parameter count is the obvious candidate and does not fit (the additive program has by far the most parameters and the second-smallest gap)
_program_numbers_replicate_held_out.SCOPE_S1700: skip11000 was previously exposed to component-level experiments; unseen by the object being tested but NOT broad OOD. See _skip11000_is_not_broad_OOD.

_attention_v1_path_stake.claim: Attention's threaded v1 path is worth 0.7066 nats under position-weighted mean ablation across all 18 modules, about a fifth of the residual write path's 3.5840 nats on the same protocol. First measurement of this path.
_attention_v1_path_stake.DEGENERATE_JOINT_ARM: the 'both' arm is identically the 'write only' arm: with all 18 attention output writes pinned to constants, v1 has no causal route to the logits (it enters only through later attention outputs). CEs agree to 5dp because they are the same computation. pred_b ('the paths are non-additive by >=10%') PASSED ON A STRUCTURAL IDENTITY, not evidence -- the LESSONS 29 shape, where a prediction about a RELATIONSHIP between arms is free when one arm is nested in the other.
_attention_v1_path_stake.not_answered: the redundancy/composition question the joint arm was meant to answer; no composition claim is made
_attention_v1_path_stake.architectural_not_discovered: v1's influence is entirely mediated by the attention writes above it -- this follows from the wiring, like the S1662 correction
_attention_v1_path_stake.NESTED_NOT_ADDITIVE: v1 is worth 0.7066 nats GIVEN a live write path and nothing without one. Combining the two numbers into a total for attention would double-count.
_attention_v1_path_stake.cross_reference_not_comparator: S1682 priced the write at 3.5570 under OPTIMAL-constant ablation; a mean constant is weaker so stakes here are larger (+0.027, expected direction and size)

_attention_write_is_mostly_two_position.claim: A least-squares map from [x_t, x_(t-1)] reproduces 56.26% of bilin18's eighteen attention output writes, against 16.38% from x_t alone. The +39.88-point gain is 32.59 points lag-1-SPECIFIC: a lag-8 control at identical parameter count reaches only 23.67%.
_attention_write_is_mostly_two_position.control: lag 8 has the same parameter count and no privileged relation to position t; a generic second slot is worth ~7.3 points, the previous position specifically ~32.6
_attention_write_is_mostly_two_position.failed_prediction: pred_b predicted attention would stay below 50% under a two-position family. It reaches 56.26%. S1682's '83.6% non-local' was a statement about the strictly-LOCAL family, not about the depth of attention's non-locality -- most of it dissolves with one position of context.
_attention_write_is_mostly_two_position.prices_at_scale: S843's previous-token finding, now at whole-stack scale: not one head's quirk but the largest single component of what all 18 attention modules write
_attention_write_is_mostly_two_position.not_claimed: that attention is a previous-token copier -- 43.7% still needs something wider, and the fitted map may use x_(t-1) for anything, not just copying
_attention_write_is_mostly_two_position.scope: attention OUTPUT WRITE only; v1 passed through unchanged (S1682, S1684)

_attention_beyond_lag1_is_diffuse.claim: Beyond the previous position, attention's output write depends DIFFUSELY on context: a spread window (1,2,4,8) reaches 68.05% while a contiguous one (1,2,3,4) at identical slot count reaches 66.71%. Sampling context widely is slightly BETTER than sampling it densely, so the dependence beyond lag 1 is 'some history', not 'the immediately preceding tokens'.
_attention_beyond_lag1_is_diffuse.controls: the empty set reproduces S1682's 16.38% and the single lag reproduces S1685's 56.26%, both exactly
_attention_beyond_lag1_is_diffuse.failed_predictions: pred_b predicted four recent positions would exceed 70% (66.71%); pred_c predicted contiguous would beat spread by >=3 points -- spread WINS by 1.34. The recency framing was wrong for every slot except the first.
_attention_beyond_lag1_is_diffuse.third_diffuse_result: S1663 (mlp1's residue across 18 heads), S1671 (the compiled program's shortfall across 18 sites), S1686 (attention's positional dependence beyond lag 1). Three grains, same shape.
_attention_beyond_lag1_is_diffuse.scope: attention OUTPUT WRITE only; v1 passed through unchanged

_attention_residue_is_content_routed_not.claim: Attention's output write saturates under fixed-position linear description at four or five slots: widening a geometric spread from (1,2,4,8) to (1,2,4,8,16,32,64) -- out to a quarter of the 256-token window -- buys only 2.03 points, and the last three doublings buy 0.82 together. The remaining ~30% is therefore NOT long-range structure a wider window would catch; it is outside any fixed-position description, i.e. content-dependent routing.
_attention_residue_is_content_routed_not.lag1_irreplaceable: removing lag 1 from the six-slot spread costs 27.90 points (69.89 -> 41.99) even with six other positions available to reconstruct it from
_attention_residue_is_content_routed_not.failed_prediction: pred_a predicted >=3 points from widening to lag 64 if the residue were long-range; it buys 2.03
_attention_residue_is_content_routed_not.scope: attention OUTPUT WRITE only; v1 passed through unchanged and worth 0.7066 nats NESTED inside the write, not additively (S1684)

_lag1_failure_is_middle_band.claim: The lag-1 positional program's shortfall is CONCENTRATED in the middle attention band. Exempt-one (recompiled per exemption): attn5 +11.60% (26.53% of the 43.74-point shortfall) against a 5.56% uniform split; best described are attn17 +1.27%, attn15 +2.91%, attn0 +2.99%. Spread across layers is ~9x.
_lag1_failure_is_middle_band.control: the no-exemption arm reproduces S1685's 56.26% exactly
_lag1_failure_is_middle_band.first_concentrated_result: after three diffuse-not-sparse findings (S1663 heads, S1671 sites, S1686 positions), attention's departure from a lag-1 description does have structure
_lag1_failure_is_middle_band.failed_generalisation: pred_a (early attention best described, motivated by S843 placing previous-token writing at attn0) PASSED by 1.48 points on its literal condition but its story is refuted by the same run: attn17 and attn15 are better described than attn0. The pattern is middle-versus-ends, not early-versus-late. Fourth prediction in this arc to pass while its generalisation failed.
_lag1_failure_is_middle_band.CONVERGENCE_with_mlp_side: the MLP middle band (mlp4-15) is the one a token table cannot describe (21.73% vs the front's 76.45%) and has the largest irreducibly-quadratic share (37.67%); the attention middle band (attn5-8) is where a lag-1 description fails worst. Two independent families, two different modules, same location: bilin18's front and back are cheap to describe and its middle is where the computation is.
_lag1_failure_is_middle_band.scope: attention OUTPUT WRITE only; v1 passed through unchanged

_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.claim: Attention's value path needs about a THIRD of its dimensions and then saturates: with real routing held exactly fixed, a rank-r least-squares map at c_v gives 67.05% at rank 256, 94.97% at 384, 98.32% at 512, 99.71% at 768, 100.01% at full rank. There is a sharp knee between 256 and 384 (27.9 points over 128 dimensions).

identity_check.note: c_v is LINEAR in x so the full-rank least-squares map recovers c_v itself; the 0.01% over is ridge-level numerical difference

_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.failed_predictions: pred_a predicted rank-64 values with real routing would clear the best fixed-position family (70.08%) by >=10 points; it reaches 2.37%, i.e. 67.7 points BELOW a family that does no routing at all. pred_b also failed.
_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.NOT_ESTABLISHED: 'routing versus values' is not a clean contrast in this design -- the positional families constrain WHICH POSITIONS may be read while leaving the read full-rank; these arms constrain the RANK of what is read while leaving routing exact. Different budgets, so 2.37% vs 70.08% prices two incomparable restrictions and cannot support 'values matter more than routing'. The defensible reading is the rank curve alone.
_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.clean_routing_statement_from_the_other_d: S1687's positional families saturate at 70.08% with full-rank values and no routing, and exact routing with full-rank values is 100% by construction, so routing is worth the ~30% S1687 identified as content-routed
_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.scope: hooking c_v also changes the v1 block 0 exports, since v1 is that same pre-mix v
_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.claim_ORIGINAL_S1689: Holding bilin18's real attention routing exactly fixed and compressing only the value path (c_v output replaced by a rank-r least-squares map of x) is catastrophic: rank 256 of 1152 gives 67.05%, rank 64 gives 2.37%, rank 8 gives -26.10% (worse than replacing attention with a constant). Exact routing does not compensate for a compressed value path.
_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.CORRECTION_S1690: S1689 read 'the value path is HIGH-RANK' off a single point at rank 256 that falls on the cliff edge. The filled-in curve (S1690, attn_value_rank_curve.py) shows a sharp knee at ~384 and fast saturation above 512. Two S1690 predictions failed in the direction of the model being MORE compressible than S1689 said. The supported statement is 'about a third of its dimensions', not 'high-rank'.
_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.controls_S1690: rank 256 reproduces S1689's 67.05% exactly; identity arm 100.01%; curve monotone
_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.vs_MLP_side: S1664 found the front MLPs' token tables reach 92-98% at rank 64 of 1152; attention's value path needs 384 for the same fidelity -- six times the rank. Both are data-weighted rank budgets on a 1152-dimensional read inside a module, both compiled bottom-up, so the comparison is on comparable footing.

_attention_value_path_is_high_rank_RENAM: see _attention_value_path_is_high_rank; the entry's claim was corrected at S1690 and the key name now overstates it

_attention_routing_is_low_rank_values_ar.claim: Under matched rank budgets on the same module (rank-r least-squares maps, data-weighted, compiled bottom-up), attention's ROUTING tolerates heavy compression while its VALUE path does not. At rank 64 of 1152 (5.6% of dims) routing keeps 62.82% of the write and values keep 2.37% -- a 60.45-point gap. The gap is 24.88 at rank 256 and closes by rank 512.
_attention_routing_is_low_rank_values_ar.FAILED_PREDICTION_pred_a: Written as 'the smallest tested rank reaching 95% of full is BELOW 384, the value path's figure'. Routing's crossing is AT 384, so the prediction FAILS. The constant was also wrong: S1690's output shows the value path reaches only 94.97% at 384 against a 95.01% bar, so its crossing is 512. The corrected comparison (routing 384, values 512) favours the claim, but a failed prediction is not rescued by fixing its constant afterwards. Recorded as a FAIL.
_attention_routing_is_low_rank_values_ar.why_the_claim_survives: crossings are a bad statistic here -- both curves are steep near their knees so one grid step moves them. The matched-rank GAPS are the evidence: +60.45, +24.88, +2.10, +0.46 as rank grows, consistent and large wherever either curve is under saturation.
_attention_routing_is_low_rank_values_ar.resolves: the routing-versus-values question S1689 opened but could not answer in comparable units
_attention_routing_is_low_rank_values_ar.combined_picture: with S1687 (positional families saturate at 70.08%, so routing is worth the ~30% they cannot reach), attention's write is a cheap low-rank SELECTION over an expensive nearly-full-rank PAYLOAD
_attention_routing_is_low_rank_values_ar.measured_in_condition: Each rank budget is applied to ONE projection group with the rest of the model running real -- a single-component statement, not a joint-program one.

_only_attention_routing_is_compressible.claim: Across four matched rank budgets in bilin18 (same fit, same bottom-up compilation, same currency), only attention's ROUTING tolerates compression. At rank 64 of 1152: attention routing +62.82%, attention values +2.37%, MLP readout (Down) -15.16%, MLP feature-forming (Left/Right) -52.88%. Left/Right is still -37.10% at rank 256.
_only_attention_routing_is_compressible.failed_prediction: pred_b predicted both MLP arms would clear 50% at rank 64 against attention's 2.37%, on the reading that attention's payload was unusually expensive. Both are NEGATIVE there. Attention's value path is the SECOND CHEAPEST of the four paths, not the expensive outlier -- this reverses the framing given in S1691.
_only_attention_routing_is_compressible.headline: a compact program can afford to approximate WHERE the model looks, but not WHAT it computes
_only_attention_routing_is_compressible.negatives_are_measurements: both identity arms return exactly 100.00% and both curves are monotone in rank -- the LESSONS 28 diagnostic for distinguishing a real negative from compounding. The substituted models really are worse than constant-ablated ones.
_only_attention_routing_is_compressible.closes_loop_with_S1679: S1679 found the 4608 bilinear features are not sparse-SELECTABLE (top 512 pinned is worse than constant ablation, because the readout sums cancelling contributions); S1692 finds the same feature-forming path is not low-rank COMPRESSIBLE either. Two different compressions, two failures, same object.
_only_attention_routing_is_compressible.measured_in_condition: Each rank budget is applied to ONE projection with the rest of the model running real. The ordering replicates held-out (S1693) but is a single-component statement; S1696/S1697/S1704 show single-component measurements do not straightforwardly predict behaviour inside a fully substituted program.

_compressibility_ordering_replicates_hel.claim: S1692's compressibility ordering replicates exactly on fineweb_n192_skip11000, untouched by the S1689-S1692 rank work: routing 62.82->63.00, values 2.37->2.29, Down -15.16->-14.42, LeftRight -52.88->-53.39. No path moves more than 0.74 points and the ordering is identical.
_compressibility_ordering_replicates_hel.pattern: house second-class confirmation (S1595, S1598, S1603; S1683 precedent); programs compiled ONCE and scored on both eval sets
_compressibility_ordering_replicates_hel.reference_arm: the skip7000 arm reproduces S1692 to +0.00% on all four paths
_compressibility_ordering_replicates_hel.document_sample_note: skip11000 is easier to predict (CE live 3.097 vs 3.292) while BOTH stakes are larger there -- the modules matter more on the easier documents. Ceilings are ratios within their own eval set, which absorbs this.
_compressibility_ordering_replicates_hel.SCOPE_S1700: skip11000 was previously exposed to component-level experiments; unseen by the object being tested but NOT broad OOD. See _skip11000_is_not_broad_OOD.

_whole_model_program.claim: A 36-piece compiled program -- a linear map of the residual stream at each of bilin18's 18 MLPs and a lag-1 map [x_t, x_(t-1)] at each of its 18 attention output writes, compiled INTERLEAVED bottom-up -- reproduces 50.94% of a 5.5684-nat joint stake (2.836 nats). First whole-model figure in this arc.
_whole_model_program.controls: the MLP-only arm reproduces S1676's 60.81% and the attention-only arm S1685's 56.26%, both exactly; the baseline CE reproduces 3.29205
_whole_model_program.halves_compound_gently: the joint ceiling is 9.9 points below MLP-only and 5.3 below attention-only. Each half's program was fitted against a real other half; absorbing the other's error costs ~10 points, not the collapse S1668 produced when independently-fitted programs were installed together (-42.99%). Interleaved compilation is the difference.
_whole_model_program.joint_stake_is_subadditive: 5.5684 against 7.8872 for the halves summed -- the S1666 CE-saturation effect (5.57 nats above a 3.29 live CE puts the model at 8.86 against a 10.82 uniform ceiling). The joint CEILING is a ratio within its own condition and is unaffected, but the joint STAKE is not additive.
_whole_model_program.scope: attention v1 passed through unchanged (S1682, S1684) -- 36 output paths replaced, not 36 modules

_baseline_needs_a_known_answer_check.claim: A ceiling is a ratio of three measured numbers and a known-answer check on one is not a check on the other two. Every identity arm in the S1659-S1693 arc constrains the SUBSTITUTION; none constrains the BASELINE.
_baseline_needs_a_known_answer_check.evidence: the first execution of whole_model_program.py measured ce_live THROUGH constant-ablation hooks registered directly on the modules, returning 8.86042 against the arc's own 3.29205. Every stake went negative, every ceiling NaN. The identity arms would have PASSED had the run reached them, because the substitution was fine.
_baseline_needs_a_known_answer_check.fix: assert abs(ce_live - published_ce_live) <= 1e-3, pinning the baseline the same way the identity arm pins the substitution
_baseline_needs_a_known_answer_check.what_caught_it: 8.86 being visibly wrong to a reader of the ledger -- the same luck that caught S1681's no-op, and luck is not a control

_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.claim: Upgrading each half of bilin18 to its best known family carries only about a third of the half-level gain into the whole-model program. The attention half gains 11.79 points alone (56.26 -> 68.05 under lags 1,2,4,8) and the MLP half up to 3.5 (tables at mlp0-2); the joint 36-site program gains 4.10 (50.94% -> 55.04%).
_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.controls: all three exact -- baseline CE 3.29205 (S1695 assert), simple arm 50.94% reproducing S1694, joint stake 5.5684 reproducing S1694
_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.failed_prediction: pred_a predicted >=8 points of the half-level upgrade would carry into the joint program; observed 4.10, a miss by 3.9 points
_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.PRACTICAL_CONSEQUENCE: half-ceilings measured with the other half real are not additive, not averageable, and not reliable even as DIRECTIONS of improvement at full scale. Budget allocated by improving one half's ceiling and assuming transfer will be over-optimistic by roughly a factor of three on this evidence.
_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.mechanism_unresolved: either the improved attention program's residual error still compounds through 18 MLP programs refit around it, or the wider lag set recovers information the MLP programs were already reconstructing from the stream so recovering it twice buys less. Both predict the observed shape; separating them needs an arm that upgrades one half at a time inside the joint condition, not run here.
_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.best_account_of_the_model: a compiled program of 18 token-or-linear maps and 18 four-position maps reproduces 3.065 of 5.568 nats (55.04%) of bilin18's 36 module output paths
_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.scope: attention v1 passed through unchanged -- output paths, not whole modules
_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.RESOLVED_S1697: mechanism identified as COMPOUNDING, not redundancy: the two single-half upgrades sum to +3.97 against a joint +4.10 (0.13-point gap), so they are additive and each is independently damped. See _half_upgrade_shortfall_is_compounding_not_redundancy.

_half_upgrade_shortfall_is_compounding_n.claim: Upgrading one half at a time inside the joint 36-site condition gives +2.66 (attention) and +1.31 (MLP) over the simple program, summing to +3.97 against a both-upgraded +4.10 -- a 0.13-point gap. The upgrades are ADDITIVE; redundancy is not detectable. S1696's shortfall is COMPOUNDING: each half's upgrade is independently damped by the other half's residual error.
_half_upgrade_shortfall_is_compounding_n.controls: simple arm reproduces S1694's 50.94% and the both arm S1696's 55.04%, both exactly

The denominator of a ceiling is a stake, so ceilings computed against one are unaffected. What it is NOT is a measure of where a program's work is, or a basis for ranking sites of different kinds against each other.

_COMPILED_PROGRAM_IS_POSITION_WISE.purpose: Scope pointer, and the most important one for reading any table+linear program figure. Established by direct measurement at S1765 and derivable from the program's own form.
_COMPILED_PROGRAM_IS_POSITION_WISE.the_fact: Every site substitute in the table+linear class is `table[token_j] + f(x_j) W` -- a function of position j's own token and own residual. At layer 0 the residual is rmsnorm(wte(token_j)), a function of token j alone. So if every site at position j is substituted, by induction over layers the ENTIRE forward at position j is a function of token j alone. Attention is the model's only cross-position path and replacing its OUTPUT with a position-wise expression removes it. The program does not approximate attention badly; it deletes attention.
_COMPILED_PROGRAM_IS_POSITION_WISE.measured: With the 36-site program installed, a +10-per-channel poke at any position changes NO later position's loss -- exactly 0.000e+00, at both a covered and an uncovered poke site. The identical poke on the live model moves later covered positions by 1.184e-01 nats (S1765, ops/poke_in_program_context.py).
_COMPILED_PROGRAM_IS_POSITION_WISE.consequence: Every recovery figure for a fully-installed table+linear program (S1747-S1758) is the recovery of a PURE PER-TOKEN FUNCTION. The best of them, +0.78536 nats of a 4.2611-nat stake at table rank 64 with a rank-128 correction, is what a map from the current token alone achieves. The remaining gap is not program quality; it is the part of the model that is about other positions.
_COMPILED_PROGRAM_IS_POSITION_WISE.not_a_bigram_though: S1766: the program beats a bigram fitted on the same 24,576 fit tokens by 1.33 nats (6.57289 against 7.90729 covered CE, skip11000), and the plain table baseline beats it by 0.55. The tables are estimated from the MODEL's activations, so they inherit per-token knowledge the fit corpus does not contain. This is a floor on what the fit data supports, not a claim about lookup tables in general.
_COMPILED_PROGRAM_IS_POSITION_WISE.explains: S1747's -0.5462 joint composition failure (installing all 36 deletes attention, installing one does not); S1751's rank saturation (no rank helps a position-wise map represent something non-local); S1764's exact covered/uncovered partition; and why S1752's partial restoration of context made things worse rather than better.
_COMPILED_PROGRAM_IS_POSITION_WISE.does_not_apply_to: S1736-S1746, which are ablation and importance results on the LIVE model, and to any program whose substitute reads other positions.

_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.claim: The exact ceiling of the position-wise program class is the model's own output given only the current token, obtained by running each of the 5419 covered tokens as a LENGTH-1 sequence. It scores 5.97902 covered CE on skip11000 and 6.03465 on skip7000, against an all-tabled baseline of 7.35825 / 7.35114 and a live model at 3.09711 / 3.29205. On the 4.2611-nat and 4.0591-nat stakes this decomposes IDENTICALLY on both roles: the class can reach 32.4% of the stake, and 67.6% is CONTEXT that no position-wise program can touch.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.why_this_is_a_ceiling_and_S1767's_was_no: The compiled program does NOT beat it (6.57289 against 5.97902). It DID beat S1767's leave-one-out bigram by 0.76 nats, because a bigram from 27k eval tokens is data-limited while the model's own per-token function is not. S1767's pred_c caught that and its pred_a/pred_b are withdrawn.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.consequence_for_the_no_go: Codex's CONTEXTUAL_COMPILER_NO_GO_AND_GATE.md prunes the position-wise grammar on a correct derivation (S1765). This gives the prune its number: the dominant term is context at 67.6% of the stake and is genuinely unreachable -- AND 0.59387 nats, 43% of what the class CAN deliver, is still unclaimed by the best program in it. The prune is right about the dominant term and it is not free.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.construction: each covered token as a length-1 sequence; log-softmax over the FULL 50,304-wide head, since slicing to the tokenizer's 50,257 would change the normalisation and the CE. Zero lookup misses on both eval roles.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.position_caveat: there is no additive positional embedding and rotary cancels for a position attending only to itself, so a self-only forward is position-independent. RMSNorm and any length-dependent statistics are NOT ruled out by a length-1 batch, so this is the model's per-token function evaluated at position 0.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.protocol: covered positions from 64, coverage mask pinned to n96_skip80 (5419 of 50257), matching every published figure in S1747-S1758
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.CORRECTED_2026_08_28_CODEX_RED_TEAM: This entry originally called 5.97902 THE CEILING of the position-wise class. That is not licensed. For the class of all position-wise predictors g(t_j) the CE optimum is the true conditional P(t_{j+1}|t_j), i.e. H(T_{j+1}|T_j); the length-1 transformer output is ONE FEASIBLE member of the class, not its optimum. Because it is achievable, its CE is an UPPER bound on the class optimum, so the bounds run the other way: the class reaches AT LEAST 32.4% of the stake, and context is AT MOST 67.6%. The 'unclaimed 43%' figure is void -- S1769's context-free tables reach this reference exactly and the distance to the true optimum is unknown. Quantifying it needs a defensible estimate of H(T_{j+1}|T_j), which S1767 showed these row budgets cannot supply.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.what_it_is: a replicated SELF-ONLY REFERENCE: 5.97902 covered CE on skip11000 and 6.03465 on skip7000, achieved by the model's own output at sequence length one. Achievable, so an upper bound on the position-wise optimum's CE.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.what_survives_unchanged: the installed program has ZERO cross-position dependence (S1765, measured at exactly 0.000e+00 and derived by induction), so it cannot recover any contextual effect. That never depended on the ceiling framing.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.CE_ONLY_SCOPE_S1788: EVERY FIGURE IN THIS ENTRY IS CROSS-ENTROPY. S1788 measured the settled standalone program with three other instruments on three roles: top-1 AGREEMENT with the live model 22.7-24.2%; top-1 ACCURACY against the true next token 13.55/14.25/13.64% against the live model's 39.32/42.35/38.88%, i.e. about ONE THIRD; and KL(live||program) 2.75-3.05, which equals the covered CE gap to within 1% (ratio 1.0010/1.0008/0.9912) so there is no hidden divergence off the data's support. 'Recovers 32.4% of the stake' and 'keeps a third of the model's next-token accuracy' are different sentences; quote both. DERIVED WITHOUT A FURTHER RUN, from S1782's bit-identity: at a covered position the full-rank program IS the length-1 model, so the CLASS REFERENCE keeps only 37.5/37.0/39.2% of the live model's top-1 accuracy. The accuracy deficit belongs to the class, not to this program, and context is worth about 25 percentage points of top-1 accuracy -- the accuracy-axis counterpart of 'context is at most 67.6% of the CE stake'. S1789 LOCATES THE DEFICIT: split by the TRUE TARGET's fit-row count, the program keeps 63.5/62.9/63.4% of live top-1 accuracy on targets seen 125+ times and 2.7/6.2/3.6% on targets never seen. The one-third aggregate is a MIXTURE of those regimes and describes neither. The concentration is the program's, not the task's: top-over-unseen accuracy ratio is 57.9/21.7/41.4x for the program against 2.4/2.2/2.4x for the live model, which is nearly flat across target frequency. 82% of the program's correct predictions come from the top bucket against 45% of the model's. Not circular - the program emits over the full 50304-wide head and is measured never to place the argmax on a rare token. S1790 QUALIFIES THE CLASS CLAIM ON THE ACCURACY AXIS: an eval-row leave-one-out bigram MATCHES the program on the 125+ bucket (program margin +1.74/+0.94/-0.93pp, failing a 1pp bar and NEGATIVE on skip1200) and BEATS it overall (15.97/16.63/18.00% vs 13.55/14.25/13.64%), while in CE the program beats the same object comfortably (6.573 vs 7.295, S1767). The program does beat the FAIR same-data bigram by +4.65/+5.18/+4.04pp overall, but the bigram's own fit-to-eval ESTIMATION gap is +7.07/+7.56/+8.40pp - larger than the program's entire advantage at every role - so the edge cannot be attributed to the architecture on this evidence. No CE figure is retracted; the reading changes. S1791 CORRECTS S1790's WORDING: the program is bigram-CLASS in accuracy, NOT bigram-identical in behaviour. Program-bigram top-1 agreement on the head is only 51.3/52.9/49.0%, far below a 70% bar; they disagree on about half of head positions. The program is nonetheless +11.0/+12.3/+9.2pp closer to the bigram than to the live model it was compiled from. Among head positions where they disagree and exactly one is right the program wins 54.0/52.1/48.2% - a coin flip - so S1790's overall deficit comes from the TAIL (10.1/24.1/10.2% of decided disagreements there), not from being wrong where it commits on the head. An oracle union of the two reaches 49.1/50.9/52.0% on the head, +10 to +12pp over either alone and still 9-12pp below live: they are substantially complementary. S1793 DISENTANGLES S1789's CONFOUND: matched on HELD-OUT frequency (leave-one-role-out) and differing only in fit coverage, the program scores 0.45/0.45/0.00% on frequent-but-uncovered targets (n 447/443/234) against 39.01/40.42/38.91% on frequent-and-covered ones, while the live model moves only 30.65/32.96/27.35% -> 61.46/64.31/61.37%. The program's limit on the tail is COVERAGE, not frequency: targets absent from the 5419-type fit set are unreachable. All four predictions passed including the cross-run control on S1789's published accuracies.

_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.COVERAGE_LEVER_PRICED_S1800: S1800 PRICES THE COVERAGE LEVER AND CLOSES IT. In the safe region (n/D 2.35-4.70, away from the n=D collapse of S1799) the curve is monotone but FLAT BY 3613 TYPES: equal +903-type steps buy +0.73/+0.76/+0.74pp, then +0.12/+0.20/+0.30, then +0.16/+0.21/+0.13 overall - a 4-5x decay, and on the head +2.80/+3.15/+2.67 falling to +0.25/+0.36/+0.25, roughly 10x. _POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.RIDGE_SCOPE_S1803: RIDGE SCOPE (S1799/S1801/S1803). The rank-64 embedding->row map's ridge is set as an ABSOLUTE 0.01*(n/D), which measures 1.38e-09 * lambda_max(Ecov^T Ecov) -- inert. At FULL coverage this costs almost nothing (best scaled ridge 0.1*lmax gains only +0.26/+0.11/+0.18pp, 0.4-1.0% of the gap) because cond(A)=324 there and the data term conditions the solve on its own. But BELOW n ~ 2D it is catastrophic: at n=D=1152 the inert ridge scores 2.40/2.51/2.28% against 11.84/12.39/11.72% for 0.1*lmax, a 9.4-9.9pp collapse. Every accuracy figure in S1788-S1802 was measured at full coverage and is therefore within 0.26pp of the best ridge in this family. The design point stands; the ridge is close to optimal AT FULL COVERAGE ONLY and must not be reused at lower coverage without rescaling to lambda_max.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.NO_MINIMAL_DEPARTURE_S1802: S1802: NO MINIMAL DEPARTURE FROM THE CLASS EXISTS. Holding one attention layer live in an otherwise fully compiled program gains at best +0.38/+0.47/+0.35pp - 1.4-1.7% of the 25.77/28.10/25.24pp gap to live. The best layers are L16/L15/L16 (LATE), which contradicts S1706's post-hoc downstream-depth story; that story does not generalise beyond the two MLP points it was fitted to. Unpredicted: restoring L5 or L6 live COSTS 12-13pp, nearly the program's entire accuracy, while L4 costs 0.03pp - a 12-point cliff between adjacent layers, reproducing on all three roles, recorded and not yet explained.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.COMPILATION_IS_DIRECTIONAL_S1806: COMPILATION IS DIRECTIONAL (S1805/S1806). Top-down (depths 0..L live, rest compiled) is cheap and well behaved: half the 25.77/28.10/25.24pp gap needs 11 live layers, keeping the bottom four live buys only 2.2/2.2/1.7%, and compiling the top seven costs under half the gap. BOTTOM-UP IS CATASTROPHIC: compiling only layer 0 loses 62.6/60.4/61.9% of the gap against 4.8/4.4/3.7% for compiling only layer 17, and compiling layers 0-3 with 4-17 live is WORSE than compiling all eighteen (by 44.8/43.2/46.9%). Mechanism is S1804's: a compiled layer BENEATH live layers feeds them a context-free stream and they explode (live L5 emits 152x its row's norm). CONSEQUENCE: per-layer marginals from either curve are increments along an ordering, NOT layer attributions - the two directions disagree by two orders of magnitude about which layer matters (L7/L8 top-down vs L0 bottom-up). A targeted partial compile chosen by per-layer cost does not work: compiling all but L6-L9 scores -43.2/-42.5/-46.0%, worse than compiling everything.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.MAGNITUDE_LINE_CLOSED_S1810: MAGNITUDE LINE CLOSED (S1804-S1810). S1804 observed that compiled rows mismatch live module output norms; S1807 showed correcting every site GLOBALLY makes the fully compiled program worse (-5.4/-5.1/-6.1% of gap) and that the poisoning is not magnitude at all (norm-matching moves the L3 bottom-up arm by 0.2pp). S1808/S1809 traced a 62-point bottom-up swing at L5 to mlp4 alone (78/79/82%, all seventeen other MLPs 0%, placement control exactly +0.00pp). S1810 then found that the SAME correction is NEGATIVE at full compile (-0.37/-0.34/-0.53pp) and that no single-site rescale helps at all (best +0.06/+0.08/+0.03pp against a 0.5pp bar). CONCLUSION: 'mis-scaled' is a property of POSITION, not of the row - a ten-times-oversized row is harmless when everything downstream is also a table and catastrophic when a live module must consume it. The settled program's row magnitudes are LOCALLY OPTIMAL at full compile.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.PARTIAL_COMPILE_FRONTIER_S1811: S1811 PARTIAL-COMPILE FRONTIER. Cost/fidelity over depth x table rank, cost in reals by the S1754 accounting (verified in-run against 224.737M and 20.531M). FOUR OF FIVE FULL-RANK ARMS ARE PARETO-DOMINATED. The all-sites full-rank program (230.087M, 13.55/14.25/13.64% top-1) is beaten by a rank-16 compile of the top eleven layers (r16_L7, 196.210M, 18.71%): 34M reals CHEAPER and +5.16pp BETTER. Also dominated: rNone_L3 by r16_L7, rNone_L7 by r16_L10, rNone_L10 by r16_L13. Only rNone_L13 survives and only because nothing costlier was measured. Spending reals on full-rank tables instead of on depth is the wrong trade at every budget tested. THE SETTLED RANK-64 ALL-SITES DESIGN POINT (S1786, 20.531M) IS NOT DOMINATED - r16_L-1 at 9.176M is cheaper but scores 11.68/12.45/12.10% against 12.88/13.49/12.89%, and the cheapest arm that beats it (r64_L3, 111.525M) costs 5.4x. Rank-64 keeps 97/97/99% of full-rank recovery at L10, so S1787's all-sites rank optimum transfers to partial compiles unchanged. S1816 DISCHARGES THE AXIS RISK: the dominance was measured on top-1 only, and re-testing on ALL-POSITION CE gives the SAME answer. r16_L7 beats the full-rank all-sites arm on CE too (5.6567/5.6179/5.6509 vs 6.0117/5.9848/6.0016, lower better) while costing 36M reals less; the same three of four full-rank arms are dominated on both axes; and the CE and top-1 Pareto sets are the SAME NINE ARMS on all three roles. This coexists with S1815's finding that CE punishes rank truncation 3.9-4.4x harder in magnitude, because the CE penalty for truncation shrinks with depth (r16 vs r64: +0.186 nats at L-1, +0.139 at L7, +0.083 at L10, +0.031 at L13) exactly as the top-1 penalty does. The axes weight the rank knob differently and agree on which designs are efficient. Costs in S1816 use the carryable map rank of S1814, so the cheap arms are priced correctly.

_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.EXPLODING_HEAD_S1818: S1818 IDENTIFIES THE EXPLODING HEAD as L5H7, the S1089 constant-bias head (one fixed vector on the massive-activation/gain dims, 86% of the stack's total bias value). _POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.INTERFACE_GAIN_REMEDY_S1821: S1806's DIRECTIONAL POISONING HAS A ONE-NUMBER REMEDY (S1818-S1821). Holding a live attention layer above a compiled stream costs up to -12.4pp (S1802). S1818 traced 85% of L5's excess output norm to head 5.7, the S1089 constant-bias head. S1819 REFUTED the pattern-dispersal mechanism: 5.7 keeps writing the SAME fixed vector (cosine +0.9990, dispersion 0.0997 -> 0.3398) 159x too large, and compilation makes attention outputs MORE position-constant globally (median 3.06 -> 0.58 at L4). S1820 repaired the cliff with nine per-head scalars (-11.88pp -> -0.05pp) and found 5.7's 85% norm share is only 15% of the DAMAGE. S1821 then showed the nine were over-parameterised: ONE scalar per layer, the live-norm-weighted mean ratio (1/132.87 at L5, 1/63.04 at L6), recovers 99.7/98.4/99.6% and repairs L6 equally well. L5's vector applied at L6 still recovers 52.5%, confirming only overall SCALE matters. NOT a contradiction of S1810: site-level magnitude is irrelevant when everything downstream is a table and nearly sufficient when a live module must consume the output. SCOPED BY S1822: the one-scalar-per-layer remedy works ONLY where the live layer's input is the fully compiled stream the gain was measured in - i.e. the single-live-layer configuration of S1820/S1821. Applying the same gains across a bottom-up split FAILS: at B3 correcting only the interface layer makes it WORSE (-44.8% -> -48.7%), and at B0 correcting all live layers is actively harmful (+37.4% -> -4.1%), because layers above the interface see a progressively more live stream, are not inflated, and dividing them by 60-130x annihilates them. What survives: at B3 and B5 the all-layer correction still converts -44.8%/-43.9% into +10.3%/+11.5%, better than compiling all eighteen, so S1806's bottom-up direction is NOT structurally blocked - the correction simply has to be measured in the configuration it is used in. S1822's raw arms reproduce S1806's published full-rank gap fractions exactly (37.4/-44.8/-43.9 vs 0.3742/-0.4484/-0.4391). S1824 CLOSES THE MAGNITUDE ACCOUNT FOR BOTTOM-UP COMPILATION. Sequential calibration (correct the interface layer, re-measure, correct the next, upward) is the best gain construction available and is best at every depth and role: B0 64.8/65.3/61.3% (vs 55.7 matched, -4.1 global, 37.4 raw). But at B3 it beats the better one-shot source by only +1.6/+1.6/+0.0 points against a 5-point bar - EXACTLY TIED on skip1200 - and recovers ~12% of the gap at B3/B5. So the deep-prefix residual (~88%) is NOT a scale error and no per-layer scalar will reach it. The single-interface case and the deep-prefix case are DIFFERENT PROBLEMS and only the first is a gain problem. Known-answer check passed: the first sequential gain equals the global gain at every depth (0.1693 vs 0.1696 at B3), forced because the interface layer sees the fully compiled stream under both constructions.

_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.claim: Building each site's per-token table from the CONTEXT-FREE value (the site's output on a length-1 sequence) instead of the per-token mean over fit contexts closes the entire 0.594-nat gap to the position-wise ceiling and dominates every program in S1748-S1758. Held out on skip11000, against the same fit-mean all-tabled baseline of 7.35825 and a 4.26114-nat stake: rank 8 recovers +0.80353 for 1.975M reals (13.1x cheaper AND +0.018 nats better than S1758's best of +0.78536 for 25.839M, 13.4x the efficiency); rank 64 recovers +1.14673 for 15.223M (46% more fidelity at 59% of the cost); full rank reaches the ceiling at +1.37925 for 224.778M.
_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.the_cause: Every table in S1747-S1758 was a per-token MEAN over the fit-row contexts that token appeared in. A fully-installed program is a pure function of the current token (S1765), so it can never use a context average; its own optimum is the context-FREE value. S1769: 36 context-free tables compose to the ceiling to -0.00002 nats and beat the best fit-mean program by +0.59389, matching S1768's unattributed gap of 0.59387 to five decimals.
_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.the_correction_becomes_unnecessary: The context-free table ALONE, with no linear correction, beats the fit-mean table WITH a rank-128 correction (5.97900 against 6.57289). The entire correction apparatus of S1748-S1758 -- 0.664M to 25.839M reals of factors, plus downstream training and rank sweeps -- was buying back an error the table itself introduced.
_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.compression_is_pure_loss: Unlike fit-mean tables, which IMPROVED under rank-64 truncation because they were overfitted to 96 fit rows (S1755), context-free tables degrade monotonically: 5.97900, 6.04503, 6.21152, 6.42299, 6.55472. _CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.CE_ONLY_SCOPE_S1788: EVERY FIGURE IN THIS ENTRY IS CROSS-ENTROPY. S1788 measured the settled standalone program with three other instruments on three roles: top-1 AGREEMENT with the live model 22.7-24.2%; top-1 ACCURACY against the true next token 13.55/14.25/13.64% against the live model's 39.32/42.35/38.88%, i.e. about ONE THIRD; and KL(live||program) 2.75-3.05, which equals the covered CE gap to within 1% (ratio 1.0010/1.0008/0.9912) so there is no hidden divergence off the data's support. 'Recovers 32.4% of the stake' and 'keeps a third of the model's next-token accuracy' are different sentences; quote both. DERIVED WITHOUT A FURTHER RUN, from S1782's bit-identity: at a covered position the full-rank program IS the length-1 model, so the CLASS REFERENCE keeps only 37.5/37.0/39.2% of the live model's top-1 accuracy. The accuracy deficit belongs to the class, not to this program, and context is worth about 25 percentage points of top-1 accuracy -- the accuracy-axis counterpart of 'context is at most 67.6% of the CE stake'. S1789 LOCATES THE DEFICIT: split by the TRUE TARGET's fit-row count, the program keeps 63.5/62.9/63.4% of live top-1 accuracy on targets seen 125+ times and 2.7/6.2/3.6% on targets never seen. The one-third aggregate is a MIXTURE of those regimes and describes neither. The concentration is the program's, not the task's: top-over-unseen accuracy ratio is 57.9/21.7/41.4x for the program against 2.4/2.2/2.4x for the live model, which is nearly flat across target frequency. 82% of the program's correct predictions come from the top bucket against 45% of the model's. Not circular - the program emits over the full 50304-wide head and is measured never to place the argmax on a rare token. S1790 QUALIFIES THE CLASS CLAIM ON THE ACCURACY AXIS: an eval-row leave-one-out bigram MATCHES the program on the 125+ bucket (program margin +1.74/+0.94/-0.93pp, failing a 1pp bar and NEGATIVE on skip1200) and BEATS it overall (15.97/16.63/18.00% vs 13.55/14.25/13.64%), while in CE the program beats the same object comfortably (6.573 vs 7.295, S1767). The program does beat the FAIR same-data bigram by +4.65/+5.18/+4.04pp overall, but the bigram's own fit-to-eval ESTIMATION gap is +7.07/+7.56/+8.40pp - larger than the program's entire advantage at every role - so the edge cannot be attributed to the architecture on this evidence. No CE figure is retracted; the reading changes. S1791 CORRECTS S1790's WORDING: the program is bigram-CLASS in accuracy, NOT bigram-identical in behaviour. Program-bigram top-1 agreement on the head is only 51.3/52.9/49.0%, far below a 70% bar; they disagree on about half of head positions. The program is nonetheless +11.0/+12.3/+9.2pp closer to the bigram than to the live model it was compiled from. Among head positions where they disagree and exactly one is right the program wins 54.0/52.1/48.2% - a coin flip - so S1790's overall deficit comes from the TAIL (10.1/24.1/10.2% of decided disagreements there), not from being wrong where it commits on the head. An oracle union of the two reaches 49.1/50.9/52.0% on the head, +10 to +12pp over either alone and still 9-12pp below live: they are substantially complementary. S1793 DISENTANGLES S1789's CONFOUND: matched on HELD-OUT frequency (leave-one-role-out) and differing only in fit coverage, the program scores 0.45/0.45/0.00% on frequent-but-uncovered targets (n 447/443/234) against 39.01/40.42/38.91% on frequent-and-covered ones, while the live model moves only 30.65/32.96/27.35% -> 61.46/64.31/61.37%. The program's limit on the tail is COVERAGE, not frequency: targets absent from the 5419-type fit set are unreachable. All four predictions passed including the cross-run control on S1789's published accuracies.

In the safe region (n/D 2.35-4.70, away from the n=D collapse of S1799) the curve is monotone but FLAT BY 3613 TYPES: equal +903-type steps buy +0.73/+0.76/+0.74pp, then +0.12/+0.20/+0.30, then +0.16/+0.21/+0.13 overall - a 4-5x decay, and on the head +2.80/+3.15/+2.67 falling to +0.25/+0.36/+0.25, roughly 10x.
