Together with S1796/S1797 (bigram complementarity real but unreachable from either arm's self-assessment) every lever inside the position-wise class is now priced and none reaches the model: the 25.8pp accuracy gap and the 2.88-nat CE gap are CONTEXT, which the class deletes by construction (S1765).
_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.RIDGE_SCOPE_S1803: RIDGE SCOPE (S1799/S1801/S1803). The rank-64 embedding->row map's ridge is set as an ABSOLUTE 0.01*(n/D), which measures 1.38e-09 * lambda_max(Ecov^T Ecov) -- inert. At FULL coverage this costs almost nothing (best scaled ridge 0.1*lmax gains only +0.26/+0.11/+0.18pp, 0.4-1.0% of the gap) because cond(A)=324 there and the data term conditions the solve on its own. But BELOW n ~ 2D it is catastrophic: at n=D=1152 the inert ridge scores 2.40/2.51/2.28% against 11.84/12.39/11.72% for 0.1*lmax, a 9.4-9.9pp collapse. Every accuracy figure in S1788-S1802 was measured at full coverage and is therefore within 0.26pp of the best ridge in this family. The design point stands; the ridge is close to optimal AT FULL COVERAGE ONLY and must not be reused at lower coverage without rescaling to lambda_max.
_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.NO_MINIMAL_DEPARTURE_S1802: S1802: NO MINIMAL DEPARTURE FROM THE CLASS EXISTS. Holding one attention layer live in an otherwise fully compiled program gains at best +0.38/+0.47/+0.35pp - 1.4-1.7% of the 25.77/28.10/25.24pp gap to live. The best layers are L16/L15/L16 (LATE), which contradicts S1706's post-hoc downstream-depth story; that story does not generalise beyond the two MLP points it was fitted to. Unpredicted: restoring L5 or L6 live COSTS 12-13pp, nearly the program's entire accuracy, while L4 costs 0.03pp - a 12-point cliff between adjacent layers, reproducing on all three roles, recorded and not yet explained.
_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.COMPILATION_IS_DIRECTIONAL_S1806: COMPILATION IS DIRECTIONAL (S1805/S1806). Top-down (depths 0..L live, rest compiled) is cheap and well behaved: half the 25.77/28.10/25.24pp gap needs 11 live layers, keeping the bottom four live buys only 2.2/2.2/1.7%, and compiling the top seven costs under half the gap. BOTTOM-UP IS CATASTROPHIC: compiling only layer 0 loses 62.6/60.4/61.9% of the gap against 4.8/4.4/3.7% for compiling only layer 17, and compiling layers 0-3 with 4-17 live is WORSE than compiling all eighteen (by 44.8/43.2/46.9%). Mechanism is S1804's: a compiled layer BENEATH live layers feeds them a context-free stream and they explode (live L5 emits 152x its row's norm). CONSEQUENCE: per-layer marginals from either curve are increments along an ordering, NOT layer attributions - the two directions disagree by two orders of magnitude about which layer matters (L7/L8 top-down vs L0 bottom-up). A targeted partial compile chosen by per-layer cost does not work: compiling all but L6-L9 scores -43.2/-42.5/-46.0%, worse than compiling everything.
_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.MAGNITUDE_LINE_CLOSED_S1810: MAGNITUDE LINE CLOSED (S1804-S1810). S1804 observed that compiled rows mismatch live module output norms; S1807 showed correcting every site GLOBALLY makes the fully compiled program worse (-5.4/-5.1/-6.1% of gap) and that the poisoning is not magnitude at all (norm-matching moves the L3 bottom-up arm by 0.2pp). S1808/S1809 traced a 62-point bottom-up swing at L5 to mlp4 alone (78/79/82%, all seventeen other MLPs 0%, placement control exactly +0.00pp). S1810 then found that the SAME correction is NEGATIVE at full compile (-0.37/-0.34/-0.53pp) and that no single-site rescale helps at all (best +0.06/+0.08/+0.03pp against a 0.5pp bar). CONCLUSION: 'mis-scaled' is a property of POSITION, not of the row - a ten-times-oversized row is harmless when everything downstream is also a table and catastrophic when a live module must consume it. The settled program's row magnitudes are LOCALLY OPTIMAL at full compile.
_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.PARTIAL_COMPILE_FRONTIER_S1811: S1811 PARTIAL-COMPILE FRONTIER. Cost/fidelity over depth x table rank, cost in reals by the S1754 accounting (verified in-run against 224.737M and 20.531M). FOUR OF FIVE FULL-RANK ARMS ARE PARETO-DOMINATED. The all-sites full-rank program (230.087M, 13.55/14.25/13.64% top-1) is beaten by a rank-16 compile of the top eleven layers (r16_L7, 196.210M, 18.71%): 34M reals CHEAPER and +5.16pp BETTER. Also dominated: rNone_L3 by r16_L7, rNone_L7 by r16_L10, rNone_L10 by r16_L13. Only rNone_L13 survives and only because nothing costlier was measured. Spending reals on full-rank tables instead of on depth is the wrong trade at every budget tested. THE SETTLED RANK-64 ALL-SITES DESIGN POINT (S1786, 20.531M) IS NOT DOMINATED - r16_L-1 at 9.176M is cheaper but scores 11.68/12.45/12.10% against 12.88/13.49/12.89%, and the cheapest arm that beats it (r64_L3, 111.525M) costs 5.4x. Rank-64 keeps 97/97/99% of full-rank recovery at L10, so S1787's all-sites rank optimum transfers to partial compiles unchanged. S1816 DISCHARGES THE AXIS RISK: the dominance was measured on top-1 only, and re-testing on ALL-POSITION CE gives the SAME answer. r16_L7 beats the full-rank all-sites arm on CE too (5.6567/5.6179/5.6509 vs 6.0117/5.9848/6.0016, lower better) while costing 36M reals less; the same three of four full-rank arms are dominated on both axes; and the CE and top-1 Pareto sets are the SAME NINE ARMS on all three roles. This coexists with S1815's finding that CE punishes rank truncation 3.9-4.4x harder in magnitude, because the CE penalty for truncation shrinks with depth (r16 vs r64: +0.186 nats at L-1, +0.139 at L7, +0.083 at L10, +0.031 at L13) exactly as the top-1 penalty does. The axes weight the rank knob differently and agree on which designs are efficient. Costs in S1816 use the carryable map rank of S1814, so the cheap arms are priced correctly.

_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.EXPLODING_HEAD_S1818: S1818 IDENTIFIES THE EXPLODING HEAD as L5H7, the S1089 constant-bias head (one fixed vector on the massive-activation/gain dims, 86% of the stack's total bias value). Per-head decomposition through c_proj, live vs fully-compiled stream, skip7000: h7 carries 85.0% of L5's excess output norm (h2 10%, h6 3%, rest <=1%), going 6657.8 -> 1057986.8 (158.9x). It was ALREADY dominant live - 19.5x the mean other head, 71.0% of the layer's output norm, rising to 84.9% compiled - so S1804's layer-level 152x is largely this one head. IMPORTANT SCOPE: the explosion is NOT concentrated by RATIO (max 240.8x at h2 vs median 34.0x, only 7.1x apart); seven of nine heads inflate >6x and four >34x, so the whole layer destabilises and h7 dominates the ABSOLUTE excess only because it starts 19.5x larger. L6's top head is h1, not h7, so the two cliff layers do not share a head. The attention-pattern mechanism (sink mass dispersing under a context-free stream) is a HYPOTHESIS fitted to existing observations and is NOT tested by this run - norms were measured, not patterns. The per-head split is exact (reconstruction residual <1e-3 in both streams).
_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.INTERFACE_GAIN_REMEDY_S1821: S1806's DIRECTIONAL POISONING HAS A ONE-NUMBER REMEDY (S1818-S1821). Holding a live attention layer above a compiled stream costs up to -12.4pp (S1802). S1818 traced 85% of L5's excess output norm to head 5.7, the S1089 constant-bias head. S1819 REFUTED the pattern-dispersal mechanism: 5.7 keeps writing the SAME fixed vector (cosine +0.9990, dispersion 0.0997 -> 0.3398) 159x too large, and compilation makes attention outputs MORE position-constant globally (median 3.06 -> 0.58 at L4). S1820 repaired the cliff with nine per-head scalars (-11.88pp -> -0.05pp) and found 5.7's 85% norm share is only 15% of the DAMAGE. S1821 then showed the nine were over-parameterised: ONE scalar per layer, the live-norm-weighted mean ratio (1/132.87 at L5, 1/63.04 at L6), recovers 99.7/98.4/99.6% and repairs L6 equally well. L5's vector applied at L6 still recovers 52.5%, confirming only overall SCALE matters. NOT a contradiction of S1810: site-level magnitude is irrelevant when everything downstream is a table and nearly sufficient when a live module must consume the output. SCOPED BY S1822: the one-scalar-per-layer remedy works ONLY where the live layer's input is the fully compiled stream the gain was measured in - i.e. the single-live-layer configuration of S1820/S1821. Applying the same gains across a bottom-up split FAILS: at B3 correcting only the interface layer makes it WORSE (-44.8% -> -48.7%), and at B0 correcting all live layers is actively harmful (+37.4% -> -4.1%), because layers above the interface see a progressively more live stream, are not inflated, and dividing them by 60-130x annihilates them. What survives: at B3 and B5 the all-layer correction still converts -44.8%/-43.9% into +10.3%/+11.5%, better than compiling all eighteen, so S1806's bottom-up direction is NOT structurally blocked - the correction simply has to be measured in the configuration it is used in. S1822's raw arms reproduce S1806's published full-rank gap fractions exactly (37.4/-44.8/-43.9 vs 0.3742/-0.4484/-0.4391). S1824 CLOSES THE MAGNITUDE ACCOUNT FOR BOTTOM-UP COMPILATION. Sequential calibration (correct the interface layer, re-measure, correct the next, upward) is the best gain construction available and is best at every depth and role: B0 64.8/65.3/61.3% (vs 55.7 matched, -4.1 global, 37.4 raw). But at B3 it beats the better one-shot source by only +1.6/+1.6/+0.0 points against a 5-point bar - EXACTLY TIED on skip1200 - and recovers ~12% of the gap at B3/B5. So the deep-prefix residual (~88%) is NOT a scale error and no per-layer scalar will reach it. The single-interface case and the deep-prefix case are DIFFERENT PROBLEMS and only the first is a gain problem. Known-answer check passed: the first sequential gain equals the global gain at every depth (0.1693 vs 0.1696 at B3), forced because the interface layer sees the fully compiled stream under both constructions.

_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.PARETO_CORRECTION_S1852: S1848's attained-ceiling object is NOT Pareto-optimal. On the common ALL-POSITION scored population, skip7000: rank-256 at 16,110 covered types costs 164.5M reals for CE 5.98851, against full rank at 5,419 types costing 230.1M for 6.01167 -- 28.5% cheaper and 0.023 nats better. Attaining the ceiling of a small covered set is a worse buy than approximating the ceiling of a large one. Coverage and rank INTERACT: tripling coverage buys -0.106 nats at full rank and COSTS +0.061 at rank 4, so neither S1800's coverage pricing nor S1849's rank ladder is a standalone lever.
